question: As of October 2022, which of the following is a Stupa site excavated in the state of Karnataka?
solution:
The correct answer is __**Sannati**__.

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/36f36cd5ece4186095afcf2ffbfb7b80cc04b6c2e3226e7477a419a9fbc96f85.png] __Key Points__

__
 
• **Sannati** is an important archaeological site located in the state of **Karnataka**, India.
 
• The site is known for the remains of a **Buddhist Stupa**, which dates back to the 1st to 3rd century CE.
 
• Sannati gained prominence with the discovery of the **Asokan edicts** and various inscriptions.
 
• The site provides valuable insights into the **Buddhist influence** and the history of the region during the ancient period.

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/f13e2ad6582c16aa62a83672e2547ad20a01fddb61962a1acce42eb9a1a99caa.png] **Additional Information__**

 
• **Sanchi:**

 
 
• Sanchi is a renowned Buddhist complex famous for its Great Stupa, located in the state of Madhya Pradesh, India.
 
• It is one of the oldest stone structures in India and was originally commissioned by Emperor Ashoka in the 3rd century BCE.
 
• The site is a UNESCO World Heritage Site and contains numerous stupas, temples, and monasteries.
 
 
 
• **Amravati:**
 
 
• Amravati, located in Andhra Pradesh, is home to the famous Amravati Stupa, also known as Mahachaitya.
 
• The stupa dates back to the 2nd century BCE and is an important site for Buddhist pilgrims.
 
• The site features intricate carvings and sculptures depicting the life of the Buddha.
 
 
 
• **Guntapalle:**
 
 
• Guntapalle is an ancient Buddhist site in Andhra Pradesh, known for its rock-cut caves and monastic complex.
 
• The site includes a stupa, chaityas, and viharas, which date back to the 2nd century BCE.
 
• Guntapalle provides insights into the early Buddhist architectural and cultural developments.
